questions.question: In Python, the 'else' block in a 'for' or 'while' loop executes only if:
options: The loop runs at least one iteration
No 'break' statement was encountered during the loop
The loop has an infinite iteration
questions.correct_answer: No 'break' statement was encountered during the loop

options: SyntaxError: else must not follow a 'for'

questions.question: Which of the following statements accurately describes the behavior of 'while True:' when combined with a 'break' statement inside the loop?
options: It will never terminate under any circumstances
It will terminate only if the break statement is executed, otherwise it loops infinitely
It automatically ends after one iteration
It requires an additional 'exit' statement to terminate
questions.correct_answer: It will terminate only if the break statement is executed, otherwise it loops infinitely
